terra.problem: Saying the ring stamped the king's name on things adds a detail not established by the passage. The ring is used to seal a decree written in the king's name.
The pockets joke has no setup: nothing suggests anyone was looking for a chain in their pockets.
The explanation simply repeats the appointment and ends with the generic observation that the queen made her own call.
The claim that Haman's letters were already out in the provinces needs a reference to Esther 3:13.
Mordecai received the ring and was appointed over the estate. Esther received the estate; Mordecai did not.
Saying the request is no longer polite adds a characterization the text does not give. Esther still addresses the king respectfully.
The change-of-address joke makes light of the threat of destruction and treats exile as a trivial move.
The claim that Haman's letters were already out in the provinces needs a reference to Esther 3:13.
The claim that Haman's letters were sealed that way needs a reference to Esther 3:12.
The claim that Haman's letters were sealed needs a reference to Esther 3:12. The explanation also presents the king's reason for permitting a new decree as certain when he does not state it.
The text says the orders were written in the people's scripts and languages, not that everybody could read them.
Writing in the people's scripts and languages does not establish that nobody would be unable to read a letter.
Calling the horses the fastest delivery available adds a comparison the text does not make.
The text does not say Haman's letters left the Jews with no way out.
The letters permit the Jews to assemble and defend themselves. They do not establish that everyone stayed and stood together.
The text does not establish that the palace was a long way from most of the Jews.
The explanation is generic and repeats that the purpose was readiness without developing the point.
The text does not say nobody was confused, or that the people saw Mordecai come out and cheered in response.
The text reports Susa's rejoicing but does not say nobody was confused or explicitly connect the rejoicing to the moment Mordecai came out.
The text says many became Jews; it does not say those people did not leave for other lands.
